markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a controlled supervision-allocation experiment: set terminal-only masking probability to **0.75**, preserving the corrected BERT4Rec baseline otherwise. This is a hypothesis, not an established improvement.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, terminal-only masking matches appended-MASK inference and could improve next-item learning; it cannot directly resolve the feedback’s unsupported assumptions about current needs. Second, example allocation differs from optimization weight: random-mask examples may supply several targets, so 75% terminal examples need not produce 75% terminal supervision. Third, existing allocation and margin probes characterize training behavior but cannot establish validation improvement; branch bookkeeping is needed to explain the intervention.

**Insights from related work.** First, BERT4Rec already includes last-item masking, making this a controlled allocation change rather than a new objective [1]. Second, cross-entropy reduction determines branch contributions; with pooled target averaging and mean random-branch target count m, the approximate terminal-only target share is 0.75/(0.75+0.25m) [2]. Third, gradient balancing research motivates measuring branch gradient magnitude and alignment, but those measurements do not establish recommendation gains [3]. Fourth, sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog results, supporting separate interpretation of host HR@10 and simulator feedback [4].

**Directions and framework.** Organize research along three levels:

| Direction | Intervention or measurement | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision allocation | Change terminal-branch probability | Tests training/inference alignment |
| Optimization contribution | Measure targets, losses, gradients | Explains local weighting and conflict |
| Behavioral dependence | Perturb permitted histories | Measures model sensitivity, not user intent |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Terminal allocation at p=0.75 — 3/7/2.** Originality: a precise intervention, but last-item masking already exists. Potential: inexpensive and interpretable, but may weaken contextual learning. Difficulty: a sampler change, but bookkeeping must preserve loss semantics.
2. **Per-example loss normalization — 4/7/4.** Originality: makes branch allocation more interpretable, but uses standard normalization. Potential: addresses target-count imbalance, but changes contextual-target weighting. Difficulty: modest loss refactoring, but variable target counts require care. Evaluate separately [2].
3. **Matched history-deletion diagnosis — 4/6/5.** Originality: connects feedback to controlled sensitivity comparisons, but perturbation analysis is established. Potential: identifies recent-history dependence, but cannot infer unresolved needs. Difficulty: needs no fitted predictor, but matched controls and uncertainty estimates add work.

**Selected experiment.** For each category, train one independent BERT4Rec with unchanged architecture, optimizer, random-mask procedure, and loss reduction. Draw the branch independently per example. In the terminal branch, replace the final real item with MASK and supervise only that position; never leave its target visible. Log branch sequence counts, supervised-target counts, and unreduced loss sums under the actual denominator. Preserve seeds, splits, 200-epoch ceiling, 200 batches/epoch, routing, and predictor consistency. Select using only host macro validation HR@10. No improvement is claimed before evaluation.

idea.description: Prespecify terminal-only masked-supervision probability p=0.75 per example in the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, preserving random masking on remaining examples and the existing loss reduction.
idea.motivation: Terminal-only supervision matches appended-MASK next-item inference. A single controlled allocation change is appropriate at early research progress and allows its effects to be interpreted without confounding architecture or loss changes.
idea.implementation_notes: Train exactly one independent model per category with preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Preserve all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, at most 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Retain the baseline reserved MASK token and prevent terminal-target leakage. At inference append MASK and read the final nonpadding position, never count-1. Preserve checkpoint/predictor-writer consistency and the ModelView interfaces. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Extend allocation diagnostics using explicit sampler branch metadata or counters; do not infer branch identity from target counts. Report unavailable measurements as null. Use only permitted histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. No additional predictor, score fusion, or independently fitted diagnostic model is introduced. The supplied backbone source is absent, so pseudocode specifies the intervention without inventing a replacement baseline.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    initialize corrected baseline with training seed 42
    for each baseline training batch:
        for each example:
            clean = baseline_training_sequence(example)
            if seeded_rng.uniform() < 0.75:
                sequence = copy(clean)
                labels = all_ignored()
                j = maximum_index_where(clean != PAD)
                labels[j] = clean[j]
                sequence[j] = MASK
                branch = TERMINAL
            else:
                sequence, labels = unchanged_baseline_random_mask(clean)
                branch = RANDOM
            record branch and supervised-target counts
        logits = model(sequence)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss_and_reduction(logits, labels)
        record detached branch loss sums under the actual denominator
        baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
    save one selected checkpoint and matching predictor architecture

inference(history, candidates):
    sequence = left_pad(truncate_for_appended_mask(history) + [MASK])
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    j = maximum_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    return model.predict_score(features[j], candidates)

originality.positive: A prespecified allocation change with explicit accounting makes a focused, interpretable experiment.
originality.negative: Terminal-item masking is already part of BERT4Rec; p=0.75 has no supplied empirical justification.

future_potential.positive: Results could motivate subsequent studies separating branch allocation, target volume, and gradient contribution.
future_potential.negative: Better objective alignment may not address the specific relevance failures described by simulator feedback.

code_difficulty.positive: The core intervention changes only per-example sampler branch selection.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct accounting requires inspecting the baseline reduction and preserving sampler, diagnosis, and inference contracts.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Includes last-item masking to address the relationship between training and next-item inference.
limitations: Does not establish p=0.75 as optimal for the supplied four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss documentation
contributions: Defines loss reductions and ignored-target handling relevant to branch contribution accounting.
limitations: The actual baseline loss implementation must be inspected before assigning an effective branch weight.

related_work.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
contributions: Motivates examining gradient magnitudes when interpreting contributions from multiple objectives.
limitations: Gradient measurements alone cannot demonstrate improved validation HR@10.
Adaptive balancing would be a separate intervention from the selected allocation experiment.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking evaluation can disagree with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator or replacing its selection criterion.
